key_insight: GUARD updates a deployed prediction model using a small amount of labeled target data plus multiple source domains, while explicitly guarding against future distribution shifts and uncertainty in the source models.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical pathway for maintaining clinical ML systems over time when full retraining is infeasible, especially in EHR settings with scarce labels and changing populations.
method: Anchors model updates to the current deployed predictor via robust multi-source transfer learning
Uses semi-supervised, adversarial optimization with double machine learning and cross-fitting to exploit unlabeled target covariates
Builds an uncertainty-aware guided group DRO estimator to combine source and target data with valid inference
evidence_signal: The paper reports simulation studies and a real-world rheumatoid arthritis EHR application over more than a decade, where GUARD stayed accurate with only a small number of labeled records per year.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the quality and representativeness of the available source populations and on assumptions behind semi-supervised causal/debiased estimation under shift.
